title: Batch mode for the eval runner
body:
Refs #1
Closes #40

## Why
Larger eval sample sizes (the flywheel wants many runs per case) should cost half. The Message Batches API is 50% of the standard price. The Langfuse capture / generated evals / review UI parts of #1 are not included; #1 stays open.

## What
- `python -m evals --batch [--batch-poll S]`: same cases, graders and results JSON.
- `aoa/batch_llm.py`: runs are multi-step loops, so `BatchCoordinator` collects every run's pending model call (it waits for a quiet moment, i.e. all runs are blocked), submits them as one batch, polls until it ends, and resolves each caller. `BatchedLLM` reuses `AnthropicLLM.build_kwargs` (cache breakpoints, ttl, thinking, schema) and `parse_message`; `AgentCore` and the loop are unchanged. A failed request fails only that run, with the API's reason.
- Results JSON gets a `batch` entry; the table says "batch mode (N requests in M batches, 50% price)".
- `AnthropicLLM.create` split into `build_kwargs` / `parse_message` (no behaviour change).
- CLAUDE.md evals section, session log.

## Evidence
Live: `python -m evals --batch --runs 1` (14 runs, `claude-sonnet-5-5`): all 14 cases pass, no hard failures, 40 requests in 4 batches (14, 12, 9, 5), 1492 s wall clock (each round took minutes), tokens 4.9k out / 95k cache read / 38k cache write at half price. Use it for big `--runs`; the synchronous mode stays the quick check.

## Testing
216 passed, including rounds of concurrent two-step "agents" grouped into exactly two batches and a per-request failure that fails only its caller.
